articles.title: FreshGauge: a freshness control plane inside the LLM gateway
articles.excerpt: Every LLM answer is a snapshot of the model's training data. Ask for a price, a current model name, a CEO, or a fine cap and you get something that was true — stated with exactly the same confidence a…
articles.body: Every LLM answer is a snapshot of the model's training data. Ask for a price, a current model name, a CEO, or a fine cap and you get something that was true — stated with exactly the same confidence as something that still is. Retrieval doesn't fix this on its own: RAG grounds an answer in documents, but nobody checks whether the document the answer leans on is two years old. FreshGauge is a Bifrost gateway plugin that does that check on the way out. Every completion that passes through the gateway gets its factual claims extracted, verified against live web evidence, scored by authority-weighted recency , and then acted on — logged, corrected in flight, or pre-empted with a dated brief before the model is even called.
articles.author: Harish Kotra (he/him)

articles.title: Your MCP server costs money to run. Here's how to charge for it.
articles.excerpt: Every call to your MCP server costs you something. Maybe it's an LLM call, a GPU minute, a scraping proxy, or a paid API you're reselling. When the caller was a human clicking a button, that was fine.…
articles.body: Every call to your MCP server costs you something. Maybe it's an LLM call, a GPU minute, a scraping proxy, or a paid API you're reselling. When the caller was a human clicking a button, that was fine. Now the caller is an agent in a loop, and it can call your tool 400 times before lunch. At some point you have to charge for it. This post walks through the three ways to do that today, with the code and the failure modes for each: Build it yourself — API keys and a balance in your own database. x402 — the agent pays per request, on-chain. A clearinghouse — a gateway handles keys, wallets, and billing, and you verify signed requests. I'll be upfront: I co-built a clearinghouse, Nexus402 , so option 3 is the one I know best.
articles.author: Nischal Dhakal

articles.title: Pipelining raised Fmax 62% but made latency worse
articles.excerpt: A short case study from an FPGA limit order book prototype. All numbers are post-route estimates from Yosys + nextpnr on a Lattice ECP5 (LFE5U-85F), not vendor sign-off. I kept optimizing for Fmax bec…
articles.body: A short case study from an FPGA limit order book prototype. All numbers are post-route estimates from Yosys + nextpnr on a Lattice ECP5 (LFE5U-85F), not vendor sign-off. The trap: Fmax is a proxy, not a goal I kept optimizing for Fmax because that was the number in my acceptance criteria. Then I computed the actual latency: Version Stages Fmax Latency Throughput Single-stage 1 95.65 MHz 10.45 ns 95.7 M/s Two-stage 2 154.58 MHz 12.94 ns 77.3 M/s Three-stage 3 155.86 MHz 19.25 ns 51.9 M/s Frequency went up 62%. Latency and throughput both got worse. The reason is simple arithmetic: latency = stages x period. Splitting the logic shortened the critical path by 1.6x, but the cycle count doubled. 2 / 154.58 MHz = 12.94 ns, which is worse than 1 / 95.65 MHz = 10.45 ns.

articles.title: Paper Trading Crypto Free: How to Test a Bot Honestly
articles.excerpt: Paper trading crypto free means running a bot on live market prices with simulated money, which makes it one of the cheapest ways to see whether a strategy holds up. It is only useful if you count fee…
articles.body: Paper trading crypto free means running a bot on live market prices with simulated money, which makes it one of the cheapest ways to see whether a strategy holds up. It is only useful if you count fees, slippage and sample size honestly, because a free demo can make a weak bot look better than it is. What paper trading crypto free actually tests Paper trading uses real prices but virtual balances. It answers one question well: does the bot's logic act on live data the way its backtest said it would? It does not prove that you could have filled those orders at those prices with real money. Several free options exist, including exchange demo accounts, TradingView replay, and simulated accounts on research platforms. The tool matters less than how you read the results.

articles.body: Introduction AI agents that can read, write, and analyze files locally are increasingly useful for developers and data workers. However, many AI tools require complex setups involving Python, Docker, or administrator rights, which can be barriers for quick experimentation or lightweight use. Nature AI Worker is an open-source Windows application designed to provide a simple, standalone AI agent interface. It connects to supported local Ollama models and cloud AI provider APIs without requiring Python, Git, WSL, Docker, or admin rights. This article explains the concepts behind such AI agents, the trade-offs involved, and how to get started with it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.

articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-317 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Nov. 20, 2026.
